author: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
text:
ParityQC Launches Parity Twine Optimizer via IBM Qiskit Functions Catalog

Applying QFT-record compilation to optimization on other paradigms.

Quantum architecture firm ParityQC has commercialized its compiler technology through the release of the Parity Twine Optimizer, launching the software module directly within the IBM Qiskit Functions Catalog. Operating on the underlying ParityQC Architecture (a generalized variant of the Lechner-Hauke-Zoller / LHZ architecture), the optimizer eliminates classical SWAP gate overhead by mapping optimization problem graphs natively onto physical QPU coupling maps.

The compiler technology was validated in recent Quantum Fourier Transform (QFT) compilation benchmarks and is engineered to optimize quadratic unconstrained binary optimization (QUBO) and combinatorial optimization algorithms across both NISQ and fault-tolerant hardware topologies. By bypassing routing SWAP networks, the Parity Twine Optimizer reduces two-qubit gate count and circuit depth, allowing larger and more highly connected problem graphs to execute on fixed hardware layouts. The compiler natively supports heavy-hex architectures (such as the IBM Heron QPU) and square-lattice topologies (such as the IBM Nighthawk QPU).

The software is available immediately through the IBM Qiskit Functions Catalog, offering a 30-day trial for IBM Quantum Network members operating on Flex or Premium access plans. Broader access to the underlying compiler continues to be served independently via ParityOS across ParityQC’s global hardware partner ecosystem.
